title: ELSS funds and Section 80C — tax saving investments
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: Under the old tax regime, Section 80C lets you deduct up to ₹1.5 lakh a year from taxable income for specified investments and payments: EPF, PPF, ELSS mutual funds, life-insurance premiums, 5-year tax-saving FDs, home-loan principal and children's tuition fees, among others. ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) is an equity mutual fund with the shortest lock-in among 80C options — 3 years — but its returns are market-linked and not guaranteed. The 80C deduction is not available in the new tax regime (the default). Do not buy a product only to save tax; choose it because it fits your goal and risk, and make sure you have not already filled the ₹1.5 lakh through EPF and insurance premiums.
summary_hinglish: Old tax regime mein 80C se saal ka ₹1.5 lakh tak income se ghat jaata hai: EPF, PPF, ELSS, life insurance, tax-saving FD, home loan principal wagairah. ELSS ka lock-in sirf 3 saal hai par returns market par depend karte hain. New regime mein 80C nahi milta.
summary_hi: पुराने टैक्स रिजीम में 80C के तहत साल में ₹1.5 लाख तक की कटौती मिलती है: EPF, PPF, ELSS, जीवन बीमा, टैक्स-सेविंग FD आदि। ELSS का लॉक-इन 3 साल है, पर रिटर्न बाज़ार पर निर्भर है। नए रिजीम में 80C नहीं मिलता।
